Press release January 26, 2000

Major increase in illicit drug use in Australia

A new Australian report, 'Australia's Young People: their Health and Wellbeing', released by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, shows major increases in illicit drug use.

Findings include:

  • More than a third of Australia's young has tried illicit drugs in the past year

  • Heroin use by 14 to 24-year-olds doubled in the three years to 1998

  • One in ten 10 young people reported using amphetamines and hallucinogens

  • 25 per cent of all youth deaths are linked to drugs
    (MarijuanaNews note: This almost certainly includes alcohol.)

  • 20 per cent of males and 10 of females aged 18 to 24 are considered drug addicts

  • Alcohol was the most commonly abused drug, with 87 per cent of 16-to 24-year-olds having recently consumed alcohol.

  • Drinking has turned to alcoholism for about 12 per cent of young men and 4 per cent of young women.

  • In the past decade, the number of 14-to 19-year-olds using marijuana rose from 21 per cent to 35 per cent.

  • In the 20-24 age group, 41per cent now use marijuana.
